title: Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation Overview
content: Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation, also called Siddhanta, is part of the Siddhanta Group. Its vision is to provide Bharatiya intellectual capital to the Global Community by creating an ecosystem for reviving, nurturing and developing Indian Knowledge Systems. The website states that Siddhanta is a Ministry of Education, Government of India, IKS Division accredited IKS Centre. Siddhanta works through a multi-pronged approach involving technology to extract and curate knowledge from authentic sources, build research capabilities, and use innovative approaches for knowledge dissemination. Its aim is to make Bharatiya knowledge accessible and actionable by wider society. The principal focus is making Bharat’s traditional Veda and Shastra knowledge corpus available and accessible to younger audiences in useful and interesting formats. The page also states that Siddhanta is developing 100+ cutting-edge transdisciplinary IKS courses for schools, colleges and universities, integrating with mainstream fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering, Management, Law, Medicine, Arts and Humanities.

title: About Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation
content: Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation, abbreviated as SKF, is described as a leading institution within the Siddhanta Group. The foundation is committed to creating robust platforms for globally relevant knowledge models rooted in the traditional Indian approach to learning. The page states that SKF emphasizes inclusiveness and sustainability and believes India’s knowledge systems and traditions hold potential to shape global thought leadership. Through curated multidisciplinary courses, SKF empowers academia with a nuanced understanding of Indian Knowledge Systems, bridging ancient wisdom with modern learning frameworks and real-life applications. Siddhanta’s vision is to build pride and confidence in current and future generations of Bharat about their own heritage of Bharatiya knowledge systems. The foundation aims to make Bharatiya knowledge available in all formats so that such knowledge drives ideas, policies and solutions in every walk of life.

title: What Siddhanta Does
content: Siddhanta, along with its associates, has built expertise in research and learning materials such as courses, text books, educational videos, publications and films on Shastras, Ancient Indian Knowledge System and Heritage, Indian History and Civilisation. The website states that Siddhanta has built ecosystems that can unearth wisdom embedded within the Indian Knowledge System and Heritage using technology tools, including in regional and classical languages, and disseminate this wisdom in relevant and contemporary formats. Siddhanta is committed to partnering with organisations that are engaged in revival of such knowledge systems in multiple Indian languages. The page also states that Siddhanta is working towards publishing journals, podcasts, blogs and providing a platform for debates to nurture and promote Indian Knowledge Systems, particularly among students and youth.

title: Siksha Education Platform Overview
content: Siksha is presented as an education initiative of Siddhanta. The website states that Indian Knowledge Systems are based on a deep understanding of the human being, nature and entire existence, making them a holistic and humane system of knowledge. Siksha presents this timeless wisdom integrated with contemporary education, guiding learners towards discovery of the self and pursuit of worthy goals or purusharthas for global well-being. The homepage invites learners to explore Indic wisdom and lists courses across areas such as Foundation, Agriculture, Arts and Humanities, Education, Law, Management, Medicine and STEM. The site describes Siksha courses as a journey into Indic education and ancient wisdom. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page. Pricing information is shown only on individual course pages where available.

title: Siksha Course Categories
content: The Siksha homepage lists course categories under All Categories. The Foundation category is described as foundational knowledge in ancient Indic principles for a solid academic and professional start. Agriculture explores ancient Indic agricultural wisdom and its modern applications in today’s farming practices. Arts and Humanities covers ancient Indic arts and humanities management strategies for modern creative industries and enterprises. Education explores Indic educational heritage and modern pedagogical approaches for a transformative learning experience. Law covers ancient Indic legal wisdom and contemporary applications in today’s legal landscape. Management is described as the fusion of modern management practices with ancient Indic wisdom. Medicine covers traditional Indic medical practices integrated with modern healthcare advancements for holistic well-being. STEM is described as a blend of ancient Indic scientific insights with cutting-edge technology for innovative solutions in STEM.

title: Aajivan Learning Experiences
content: Aajivan is described as Siddhanta’s set of 1-hour capsule learning experiences in multiple subjects. The listed subject areas include Design, Health and Wellness, Economics, Management, Sciences, Psychology, Governance and others, all anchored in Indian Knowledge Systems and Indic traditions. The website states that these courses are rooted in ancient insights but designed for modern living and applications, encouraging learners to research, reflect and apply. It presents Aajivan as lifelong learning made meaningful. The page says Aajivan courses are for people curious about Indian Knowledge Systems, Indic heritage and traditions, students looking to add value to their chosen subject of study, and lifelong learners. Aajivan is described as more than a course: it is a platform to refresh thinking, kindle curiosity and transform outlook.

title: Sandhaan Technology Overview
content: Sandhaan is presented as Siddhanta’s technology initiative with the statement “Making Bhaaratiya Vijnan Come Alive.” The page describes it as a collaborative effort to collect, digitize, preserve and cross-link textual sources of Bhaaratiya, or Indic, Knowledge Heritage into a reliable, open and searchable Internet repository. Bharati Kosha is explained as an electronic repository of Indic knowledge literature or Bhaaratiya Vijnaanam captured in text and other media in an intelligible form for students, researchers and enthusiasts to consult, study, reference and analyze. The repository is designed as a joint effort with Sanskrit institutions and sponsors at a national level. Areas listed include Vedic knowledge resources, Non-Vedic Buddhist and Jain knowledge resources, Shastras and commentaries, Sampradayas of Bharat, folklore and indigenous literature, Sahitya of Bharat and Agamas and temple literature.

title: Siddhanta Kosha
content: Siddhanta Kosha is described as a web portal for searchable and semantically annotated Bharatiya books. The page states that it offers paid subscription based access to consumers and remuneration to content curators who curate, enrich and annotate its content. The website explains that Bharatiya knowledge is embedded in millions of manuscripts, some printed and mostly handwritten, across diverse fields including technical, religious and social areas. A major challenge identified on the page is making these works available as processable text in Indic languages for the use of technologies such as ChatGPT. The site notes that Indic languages are grammatically different from English but share a rich grammatical structure derived from Sanskrit. It says grammatical annotation, including splitting sandhis and samaasas, can help further linguistic processing and semantic knowledge extraction.

title: Shastra Maps
content: Shastra Maps is described as enabling conceptual exploration of Indic Shaastra texts. The page presents an abstract of a research paper by Vedavaapi published at the 18th World Sanskrit Conference 2023 under the Computational and Digital Humanities section. The abstract states that Indic shaastra texts use a rigorous, structured style of discourse based on conventions of Nyaaya and Mimaamsa. Because of this structure, these texts are more amenable to mechanized navigation and interpretation than modern scientific treatises that use free-form natural language. The paper contributes a conceptual network representation called Shaastra Map and a graph query scheme called ShaastriQL. ShaastraMap is described as an overlay directed graph of sentences and sections of one or more Shaastra texts linked through relations used by shaastra authors and experts, such as tantrayuktis and padaartha sambandhas.

title: Shodha Research Wing
content: Shodha is presented as Siddhanta’s research wing, focused on unlocking timeless wisdom from Bharatiya Shastras. The page states that Shodha continuously engages with scholars and experts in Bharatiya Shastras to make Bharat’s timeless wisdom accessible and usable to contemporary audiences. Using technology tools to research primary Shastra granthas, Shodha attempts to map concepts from various Shastras that contribute to transdisciplinary learning resources and applications. The page highlights four areas: Transformational Bharatiya Pedagogy, Siddhanta Prastuti, Indic Thought Models and Conscious Enterprise Management. These areas connect learner distinctiveness, access to traditional Shastra granthas, conceptual models from Bharatiya Shastras and Darshanas, and Bharatiya management education anchored in Shastra-based models.

title: Contact Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation
content: The Contact page is titled “Get in Touch with Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation.” The page displays a contact form and asks users to enable JavaScript in the browser to complete the form. The visible form fields are Name, with First and Last fields, Email, and Comment or Message. The page includes a Contact Us button. No phone number is shown on this page. No direct support email is shown on this page. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page. Pricing information is not shown on this page. The page footer links to Home, Education, Technology, Research, Contact, Terms of Use, Privacy Policy, Refund Policy and Copyright Policy, and shows links to social media platforms.

title: Refund Policy
content: Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation’s Refund Policy states that all purchases of courses and related educational materials are final. Due to the nature of digital content and services, the page says Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation does not offer refunds on any courses or related products once a purchase has been made. The policy also mentions exceptions: while refunds are generally not provided, exceptional circumstances may warrant a refund request. In such cases, users are asked to contact the support team with a detailed explanation. Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation will review the request case by case and make a determination at its sole discretion. The contact information listed on the page is Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation, 72, Marshalls Road, Egmore, Chennai 600008, India. The page lists GST: 33AAQCS8964E1ZU and states that the policy is effective as of 07 Sep 2024.

title: Privacy Policy
content: The Privacy Policy states that the website records visit information for statistical purposes, including the server address, top-level domain from which the user accesses the Internet, browser type, date and time of access, pages accessed, documents downloaded, and the previous Internet address from which the user linked directly to the site. The policy says users and browsing activities will not be identified except when a law enforcement agency may exercise a warrant to inspect service provider logs. The site uses cookies. The policy states that an email address is recorded only if the user chooses to send a message, and it will be used only for the purpose for which it was provided. The page also states that Siddhanta takes steps to protect shared information, uses technology and security features, and secures data in transit and at rest.

title: Terms of Use Overview
content: The Terms of Use apply before registering for an account on siddhantaknowledge.org or using any portion of the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation website or mobile applications. The Terms define the Siddhanta Knowledge Site as all content and pages within the siddhantaknowledge.org web domain and all Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation mobile applications, including course material, chat rooms and other electronic services. By using the site, users accept and agree to be legally bound by the agreements, whether or not they are registered users. The Terms state that Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation may modify the Terms of Use at any time without advance notice, with changes effective immediately when posted on the page. The English language version controls if there is a conflict with versions in other languages. The effective date shown is 1-08-2024.

title: Rules for Online Conduct
content: The Terms of Use state that users are responsible for their own use of the Siddhanta Knowledge Site and for their User Postings. User Postings include content submitted, posted, published or distributed on the site by users, such as forum posts, wiki edits, notes, questions, comments, videos and file uploads. Users must use the site in compliance with the agreements and applicable laws, including copyright laws and Indian laws governing the matter. The Terms prohibit use of the site in a way intended to damage, disable, overburden or impair Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation servers or connected networks. Users may not attempt to gain unauthorized access to the site, accounts, computer systems or networks through hacking, password mining or other means. Registered users must not share their password or allow others to access or compromise their account.

title: Copyright Policy
content: The Copyright Policy states that all materials appearing in the video, including audio, visuals, scripts, presentations, expressions and intellectual work, belong to the rightful owner, Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation. The policy says nothing in the video shall be copied, altered or used in any manner without explicit prior written permission of the rightful owner. It also states that non-compliance shall be punishable under the provisions of the Copyrights Act, 1957. The disclaimer says that during the making of the material, certain images and other content available in the public domain may have been used. The page states that appropriate efforts have been made to acknowledge rightful ownership with due credits and that such public domain content is adopted solely for better understanding of viewers. The page ends with “All rights reserved © SKF.”

title: Indic Predictive Science – Advanced
content: Course title: Indic Predictive Science – Advanced. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG. Categories shown: Arts and Humanities, Management, STEM. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course offers an in-depth study of the Indian Knowledge Ecosystem with a focus on advanced Indic predictive sciences such as Medical Astrology, Agricultural Astrology, Vastu Shastra, Spiritual Astrology, Disaster forecasting and Muhurta Shastra. It is tailored for graduate students and bridges ancient wisdom with contemporary applications, addressing academic and professional needs. The syllabus includes prior knowledge, history of astrology, Panchanga knowledge, Muhurta calculations, predictive science in mundane life, Samskaras, marriage compatibility, human personality from Jyotisha, relationships, Stri-Jataka, Yogas, planetary conjunction, education, career planning, spiritual astrology, medical astrology, agricultural astrology, Vastu, water deriving, defence strategy, disaster predictions, weather forecasting, Ayanamsa, modern science and remedies. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Science of Art and Aesthetics
content: Course title: Science of Art and Aesthetics. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course is described as a comprehensive undergraduate course tailored for students in Design, Architecture and related fields. It covers the essence of beauty through Eastern and Western perspectives on aesthetics, art and philosophy. It engages with foundational texts, philosophical frameworks and practical applications to deepen understanding of aesthetic principles. The syllabus includes Foundations of Aesthetics, Vedic Principles of Beauty, Western Aesthetics, Philosophical Foundations of Aesthetics, Comparative Analysis of Subjectivity and Objectivity, Vedas and the Aesthetics of Nature and Art, Upanishadic ideas of Beauty and Ananda, Nāṭyaśāstra, Design Thinking, Human-Centered Design Principles, Prototyping and User Testing, Pratibhā, imagination in art, Aucitya, propriety, unity and congruence. Intended outcomes include understanding Indian and Western aesthetics, cultivating critical thinking and applying Design Thinking to complex design problems.

title: Indian Knowledge Systems and Traditions
content: Course title: Indian Knowledge Systems and Traditions. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course provides background to Indian knowledge systems and traditions and their relevance in sciences, technology, literature and arts. It is curated for all academic disciplines as a foundational program. The course enables understanding of India’s knowledge framework, its genesis, evolution and key components, and is described as an essential first step before deeper discipline-specific concepts aligned with career fields. The syllabus includes the importance and stature of knowledge in the Indian world, foundations of knowledge in the Vedas, chaturdasa-vidyasthanas apart from the four Vedas, chatusshashti kalaas, structure and content of the four Vedas, Vedangas such as Siksha, Nirukta, Vyākaraṇa, Jyotiṣa, Chandas and Kalpa, Upavedas, Ayurveda, Gandharvaveda, Dhatuvada, Indian architecture, temples and town planning. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: The Science and Art of Music
keywords: The Science and Art of Music
content: Course title: The Science and Art of Music. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The course introduces various aspects of Indian music in general and Karnataka-sangītam, or Carnatic music, in particular. It is foundational for all streams and especially relevant to Humanities programmes on Fine and Performing Arts. The course covers music from historic, musical and technical perspectives, including śāstra-based thought processes and contemporary practice of Karṇāṭaka-sangītam. It includes study of Sangīta Ratnākara, a musical treatise authored in 1300 CE, as a reference point to discuss and understand the development of Indian music. The course also includes listening activities to help learners experience the melody and aesthetics of Karṇāṭaka-sangītam, recognition of tonal patterns and melodic forms, and understanding of technical and śāstra-based aspects.

title: Indic Predictive Science - Basic
content: Course title: Indic Predictive Science - Basic. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course presents Jyotiṣa, often referred to as Vedic Astrology, as a profound Bhāratīya Predictive Science involving interpretation of celestial movements and their influence on human life. Key highlights include the Bhāratīya approach to predictive sciences, historical and cultural significance of Jyotiṣa, basics of Jyotiṣa with precise mathematical calculations to understand planetary positions, and a foundation for advanced predictive methodologies in fields such as science, geology, water conservation and people management, as well as life domains like career, relationships and health. The syllabus includes creation of the universe and purpose of astrology, the landscape of Jyotisha, the concept of time, time reckonings, steps of consultation and Janma Kundali. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Basic Principles of Arthashastra
content: Course title: Basic Principles of Arthashastra. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Arts and Humanities, Law, Management. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The course describes the Arthaśāstra as an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy and military strategy, traditionally attributed to Chanakya, also known as Kauṭilya or Viṣṇugupta, who was an advisor and prime minister to the first Mauryan emperor Candragupta. The course highlights understanding the Arthaśāstra landscape divided into 15 Adhikaraṇas and introduces a comprehensive approach to governance through analysis of the elements that constitute a State. The syllabus begins with Introduction and Overview of Artha Shastra and includes comprehensive insights into Artha Shastra for modern governance and leadership, historical significance, evolution and contemporary relevance, and Sattvam and Leadership. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Samskrit 1: Thinking in Samskrit
content: Course title: Samskrit 1: Thinking in Samskrit. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The course facilitates engagement with the Sanskrit language. Its key highlights include the structure of simple Sanskrit sentences, introduction to the Devanāgari script and reading of classical literature in Sanskrit. The syllabus includes introductory Sanskrit expressions and pronouns such as अहम्, भवान्, भवती and त्वम्, simple present tense, negation and questions, locative expressions such as अत्र, तत्र and कुत्र, sixth case, spatial expressions, present tense, imperative and request forms, body parts, numbers, time, verb usage, seventh case, expressions of time, past tense usage, prefixes, second case, future tense, fifth case, adverbs, ktvā and lyap suffix forms, indeclinables, fourth case, purpose expressions, third case and address forms. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Science of Language
content: Course title: Science of Language. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Arts and Humanities, STEM. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course focuses on the scientific aspect of language, specifically Vyākaraṇa. Key highlights include an overview of languages and their grammatical aspects, a deep dive into the Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini, terminology associated with Pāṇini’s treatise and the Prakriyā methodology given in Aṣṭādhyāyī for the etymology of words. The syllabus includes entering into the course through questions such as what science, language and Vyākaraṇa mean; generation of sounds and meaning of sound and words; propagation of sound, frequency, intensity, sonic, subsonic, supersonic and resonance; phonemes, graphemes and morphemes; semantic and pragmatic meaning; māheśvarāṇi sūtrāṇi and pratyāhāra; and sūtra or aphorisms. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Samskrit2 – Understanding Texts
content: Course title: Samskrit2 – Understanding Texts. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The course focuses on Sanskrit language skills to analyze prose and poetic literature. Key highlights include understanding the principles required for analyzing literary works in Sanskrit, developing skills to navigate texts using grammatical and rhetorical tools, and illustrative examples from selected verses of Bāla-Rāmāyaṇa. The syllabus begins with Unit 1 on usage of Vibhaktis. Topics include understanding the application of Vibhaktis in sentences, analysis of Karaka and Upapada Vibhaktis, exploration of Sati-Saptami and Visheshya-Visheshana relationships, application of Vibhaktis in phrases such as vina, antareṇa and dūre, and Sanskrit topics including विभक्तीनां प्रयोगाः, कारक-विभक्तीनां सम्यक्तया अवगमनम्, उपपद-विभक्तीनां ज्ञानम्, सति-सप्तमीप्रयोगस्य अवगमनं and विशेषण-विशेष्यभावः. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button.

title: Bharatiya Knowledge Ecosystem
content: Course title: Bharatiya Knowledge Ecosystem. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Category shown: Foundation. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course states that ancient Indian knowledge is poised to drive the evolution of next-generation knowledge platforms and steer global thought-leadership with Bhāratīya dṛṣṭi and ethos. It is curated for all academic disciplines as a foundational programme. The course covers India’s knowledge framework, its genesis, evolution and key components. It is presented as an essential first step to navigate Indian Knowledge Systems meaningfully and set context for discipline-specific concepts aligned with chosen career fields. It provides a bird’s eye view of India’s traditional knowledge corpus and a contextualised and contemporised view with respect to sciences, technology, literature and arts. The syllabus includes Foundations and Applications of Indic Knowledge and concepts of knowledge, including their evolution in contemporary contexts.

title: Scientific Thinking - Knowledge Modelling
content: Course title: Scientific Thinking - Knowledge Modelling. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Foundation, Management, STEM. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course uncovers the essence of scientific thinking and the process of knowledge creation. It covers model-based reasoning, anatomy of models and systematic model-building methods of Bharat with real-life applications. The course enables contextualization of Śāstras as potent scientific models with versatile contemporary applications and aims to empower learners with precision thinking and critical evaluation. The syllabus includes knowledge versus knowledge system, what science is, methods and tools of science, model building, empirical versus theory-based models, science versus art, approximate versus exact sciences, strengths and limits of scientific inquiry, the subjective element in science, models as compact representations of observed reality, types of models, abstraction and classification, explanation, prediction and control, and assessment of model quality. Outcomes include understanding model-based reasoning and assessing robustness of scientific models according to Śāstras.

title: Structures and Methods of Bharatiya Knowledge
keywords: Structures and Methods of Bharatiya Knowledge
content: Course title: Structures and Methods of Bharatiya Knowledge. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG. Categories shown: Management, STEM. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The curriculum provides an overview of the structures and methods of Bharatiya knowledge systems, focusing on the topography and classification of Indic knowledge disciplines. It is designed as a foundation course for undergraduate and postgraduate students and aims to address current academic requirements and future professional needs. The course develops understanding of the structuring of Bharatiya technical treatises. The syllabus includes introduction to Bharatiya technical treatises, purpose and importance of the course, methods and parameters of testing Shastras, reasons to avoid translations, differences between Vidya, Darshanam and Shastram, Paribhasha or technical language, structure and content of treatises, functions of Shastras, laws explaining natural phenomena, objects of study in a Shastra, general and exceptional rules, and descriptive versus prescriptive nature of Shastras.

title: Indian Reasoning and Debating
content: Course title: Indian Reasoning and Debating. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Foundation, Law, Management. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course enables exploration of the rich tradition of debate exchanges, definitions and classification systems found in Bhāratīya Śāstras. It develops skills to become a persuasive communicator with the ability to defend statements using clear and logical reasoning, choose relevant statements for defence, and support arguments with well-chosen, explanatory and thoroughly analyzed evidence. The syllabus starts with Introduction to Indian Reasoning and Debating Techniques. Topics include Bharatiya Knowledge Systems, 14 and 18 Vidyasthanas, Vedas, Vedangas, Darshanas, Astika and Nastika systems, Nyaya Shastra, Gautama, Nyaya as Darshana, Nyaya as Vada Shastra, Prachina and Navya Nyaya, theory of evidence or Pramāṇa, direct knowing through Pratyaksha, indirect knowing through Anumana, Upamana and Shabda, cognition, Prama, Prameya and Pramana, and Laukika and Alaukika Pratyaksha.

title: Philosophy of Language
content: Course title: Philosophy of Language. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Arts and Humanities, STEM. Price shown: $75.00 (Fee additional). The course provides insights into the analysis of language as a tool of communication and as a window into the working of the mind in the Indian tradition. Key highlights include a holistic overview of various aspects of knowledge, emphasis on rigorous analysis and practical veracity in accepted tenets, and understanding language as a tool for scientific inquiry and logical reasoning. The syllabus includes Introduction to Language in Sanskrit Tradition, types of Vak in the Vedas, four out of six Vedangas dealing with language, Vyakarana in India as an advanced science of linguistics, grammarian traditions before and after Panini, theory of śabda or sound and word, nature of sound, articulate and inarticulate sounds, phonetics and phonemes, nature of meaning, relation between word and meaning, power of the word, denotative power, secondary meaning and suggested meaning.

title: Indian Vision for Human Society
content: Course title: Indian Vision for Human Society. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG/PG. Categories shown: Foundation, Arts and Humanities. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course explores India’s philosophical, ethical and practical lessons that show how individual existence can harmonize with a universal rhythm. Key highlights include insights into the concept of vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam, meaning the world is one family, understanding universality of existence and oneness, and fostering a sense of duty and active participation in building an inclusive society centered on holistic well-being. The syllabus includes non-duality in Prakriti and Purush, the five great elements or Pancha-mahabhutas, roots of sorrow and suffering, pursuit of salvation and eternal peace, acceptance of various philosophical systems in ancient India, the four Purusarthas of Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha, Abhyudaya and Nihsreyasa, Dharma Sutras and Shastra, stages of life, Atman-Brahman, Koshas, Prana, Vidya and Avidya, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, Patanjali's Yoga Sutras and societal harmony.

title: Indian Town Planning and Architecture
content: Course title: Indian Town Planning and Architecture. Duration: 30 Hours. Applicable audience: UG. Categories shown: Arts and Humanities, Management. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The course provides an overview of India’s rich cultural and architectural heritage and examines how socio-cultural, economic and environmental factors influenced architectural developments. Through analysis of design principles, temple evolution and the integration of visual and performing arts in architecture, students develop critical thinking skills, appreciate the legacy of ancient Indian architects and gain practical knowledge for modern architectural practice. The syllabus section says Unit 1 is Coming Soon. Learning objectives include understanding the interplay among human societies, natural landscapes and architectural configurations in ancient India; developing critical thinking through study of socio-cultural, economic and environmental impacts on architecture; and appreciating the cultural legacy and inventive methodologies of ancient Indian architects. Outcomes include practical knowledge for modern architectural practice and evaluating architectural techniques and design principles.

title: Ayurveda: The Science of Wellness- Basic
content: Course title: Ayurveda: The Science of Wellness- Basic. Duration: 15 Hours. Applicable audience: UG. Category shown: Medicine. Price shown: ₹2,500.00 (GST additional). The curriculum provides a comprehensive overview of Ayurveda as an Indic science of life. It explores foundational principles and underlying philosophy of Ayurveda and is designed specifically for undergraduate and postgraduate students to address academic requirements and future professional needs. Each module is created to develop awareness about Ayurveda and its application for physical, psychological, spiritual and social wellbeing of an individual. The course is described as an introspective journey that reveals the eternal wisdom of Ayurveda through the Bharatiya lens and unlocks the potentials of body, mind and soul to optimize performance in everyday life. Learning objectives state that this is a basic-level course introducing fundamental principles and key concepts of Ayurveda. Outcomes include exposure to principles of Ayurveda according to Charaka Samhita and Sushruta Samhita, contemporary relevance, intellectual enrichment and a holistic perspective on health and wellbeing.

title: Arthasastra: Indic Science of Governance
content: Course title: Arthasastra: Indic Science of Governance. Category shown: Aajivan. Price shown: original price ₹499.00 and current price ₹99.00, including GST. The page shows a “Click To Enroll” button. The course explores Arthaśāstra as a living framework for leadership, redefining Artha as sustainability, clarity and purpose, not only material gain. The course page does not show course duration, credits, course code, detailed syllabus, eligibility or learning outcomes. Enrollment steps are not shown on this page beyond the “Click To Enroll” button. The page also suggests related Aajivan courses such as Designing with Aucitya: The Science of Propreity in Indian Aesthetics and Applied Ayurveda: Personalizing Your Well-Being. The page footer invites learners to embrace Indic wisdom and contact Siddhanta for more information.

title: Bharatiya Science Foundations Minor Degree Program
content: Program title: Bharatiya Science Foundations. Program type shown: Indian Knowledge Systems - Minor Degree Program. The page states that Siddhanta offers Minor Degree Programs integrating Indian Knowledge Systems into modern education. These programs blend ancient wisdom with contemporary relevance and provide students with a holistic understanding of Bharatiya traditions. Courses are described as transformative, offering foundational knowledge, specialized insights and practical applications rooted in IKS.
